collection.credit:
NEW EVENTS — JUSTICE AND CONSEQUENCES (JUS-01 to JUS-50, draft for the owner, 2026-11-15)
Everyday rules, disputes between neighbors, the elders and the council, making things right, losing a role, a night to cool down, wrongful suspicion and evidence that doesn't add up. Consequences are proportionate and never cruel; children get guidance; nobody goes without food, water or shelter; an accusation is not guilt.
Written in the style of the owner's own events. Edit anything and send it back; nothing ships until you approve.

collection.description: After a shouting match, a villager agrees to spend the night alone to cool down: sit with them a while, or leave them in peace.

setup.name: The setup
setup.text: (subject) and (friend) had a furious shouting argument at the fire tonight about a fishing spot. Nobody was hurt, but the children were frightened, and (subject) is still pacing up and down, wanting to go and have it out with (friend) all over again. The elders have asked (subject) to spend the night alone in the empty storehouse, until morning, when everyone is calmer. (subject) doesn't like it, but agrees.

o1.name: Outcome A
o1.text: (elder), an elder, brings a blanket, water and food, and sits by the storehouse door for a while. They don't talk about the argument. They talk about fish, and stars, and nothing much. (subject) calms down slowly. In the morning the elders hear both sides properly. (subject) says (subject.he/she) is still angry, but that (subject.he/she) frightened the children, and that wasn't right.

text_only.reason: food in the story (a meal, a catch, fruit); the village's stores do not change -- the draft's notes: everything but the marked effects is story only

o2.name: Outcome B
o2.text: (subject) is given a blanket, water, food and a lamp, and left alone, with (elder), an elder, close enough to call. (subject.He/she) is furious for an hour, then tired, then quiet. In the morning (subject.he/she) comes out and goes straight to the children to say sorry for the shouting. (subject.He/she) doesn't say sorry to (friend). That argument isn't finished. But this time it waits for the elders.
